![Agricultural land across the study area in Namibia, South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini.](../images/southern-africa-landuse-map.jpg){width="65%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="Map of southern Africa showing agricultural land in dark grey and non-agricultural land in light grey across Namibia, South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini."}

Soil properties mapped consistently with depth across Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa, so that maps no longer jump at every layer boundary. The research formed part of [Soils4Africa](https://www.soils4africa-h2020.eu/), an EU Horizon 2020 project building an open-data Soil Information System to help farmers, agri-businesses, scientists and policymakers by improving the quality and availability of African soil data.

Sampling was sparse, only two horizons were sampled per profile, and the environmental gradients were extreme, so we developed a new method for the project: Integrated Soil Profile Mapping (ISPM). It builds on our earlier physics-informed depth spline ([phySpline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2026.181621)) and is now being extended to update existing soil maps and support decisions. See [Now: cumulative knowledge](cumulative-knowledge.qmd). 

**Preprint:** [Integrated soil profile mapping reveals regional patterns of soil condition across Southern African agricultural lands](https://doi.org/10.31223/X5JN5T)
